column4: Visit note | 2025-11-08 10:00 AM | Dr. Shirin Akter, Pulmonology | Patient: Nupur Sarkar, 71, female. Mrs. Sarkar returns for a review of her breathing and notes a long history of smoking and wheezing on walking. She is a tailor whose symptoms flared after rubbish was burned near home in Noakhali. She reports persistent cough with scant phlegm but denies chest pain or fever. On examination: SpO2 92%, BP 123/84 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 86 kg. Chest auscultation reveals diffuse expiratory wheeze and prolonged expiration. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-11-08 10:30 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Jewel Uddin, 76, male. Mr. Uddin presents for evaluation and states he experiences brief spinning when turning in bed and nausea with the spinning. He is a retired civil servant and mentions these episodes began after a viral cold in Mymensingh. He denies hearing loss, double vision, or limb weakness. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the left side, BP 111/79 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 86 kg. Cranial nerves are intact and gait is steady. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
